title: Gut-bucket clarinet and the drummers he worked with
summary: Barnes says he drove bands to play, names drummers such as Black Happy and Dave Bailey, and praises Dave's lively drumming.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well I've heard a lot of the musicians around town talk about you as being a guts clarinet player, you know, played with more feelings than some of the others. Who were some of the other clarinet players that played on that style?

Well really I don't think I could answer you on that. Because my playing was partly different, as I first said. You see I wouldn't play one way. Contour band, this is what I thought that band was playing, and it was fitting that it was coming out right, that's where I went.
Well what were some of the bands that could really gut it?

Well you had a good many bands with gut, you see, after they get on the stand about two hours and they'd warm up, no telling what they was going to do. You understand? They'd get on and gut, you catch all of them in the gut. Now I had a habit, me and I'd make a man play. That was me always, you see I always had that feeling to play. And that man if he'd be drowsing and pulling back, well he'd wake up right now. Then I had a feeling I'd always get to my drum. When I got to my drum and get to working with my drums and my piano, I knew they was going to work there. They'd pull them. They'd be like, you know, I'd always get to work there. I'd always get to work there. I'd always get to work there. I'd always get to work there. What drummers did you like to work with? Well I had pretty good drummers, most every drum I worked with. Yeah, I had pretty good drummers, most every drum I worked with. I worked with Happy, Benny, Red Happy, a little happy to be up here, which is the Red Happy anyway. And this Happy used to be up here, with Bill. Which Happy?
Black Happy. And I worked with Benny, Dave Bailey, Cy Frazier, and Faith So. I don't know, I worked with the Grocey, everything they had here. Every drummer had a record. I worked with them.
Who did Dave Bailey play with?
Dave played with many bands, many, many bands. You might say he plays with I believe the Rinker Band now. Gibson.
Gibson? Yeah, a non-union band. Non-union?
That's who he played with? Well he's a good drummer. He was a good drummer, I can tell you that.
He was lively and still, you know.

Well on the stand, on the music stand, he stood lively. He stayed there and he danced on them drums and he had everything going and his temper was there and he never nausea out. Never get up on that cymbal and swing your eye on him, man. He worked that cymbal in there, he stood there dancing on him, he exploded like a fool and bust out and laughed. He said, he said, how about you, brother-in-law, let's go. He's gone now. Last time my son, I said no, he said he ain't playing nothing, just one or two tunes, he ain't been playing with no bands or nothing. He said you like to work with the banjo. Who are some of the different banjo players that you played with? Well I worked with many, many banjos. Little Dad and well my cousin, you know that. And uh... Which cousin? Lawrence. Wake with Lawrence and wake with John too. Lawrence is way behind, Lawrence is wake with John in my class.
